HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? candidateDecisions.label: Cumulative European-language proficiency
candidateDecisions.assessment: The workbook supports beginner Dutch for everyday use. It has no cumulative proficiency sequence in any of the eight languages and no German-medium sequence in linguistics, literature and politics. Analysing texts, speech or bilingual learning cannot supply that progression.

analysis: The closest route directly responds to the language strand through beginner Dutch, stylistics and psycholinguistics and uses rhetorical analysis and applied communication for language in public life. Modern History and European Union Politics supply regional context. Introductory brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics, which is only offered in the first spring. Qualitative methods move after introductory sociology and Rhetoric in Action moves to the final spring. The literature route has dedicated work in literary genres, theory, memoir, film and documentary. The description-only Renaissance Italy and Writing Art’s Histories strengthen its progression from close interpretation in a European setting to advanced inquiry about visual meaning and identity. The politics route preserves Modern History, comparative politics, European Union Politics and related sociology. The American Century seminar is complementary training in primary-source research rather than study of European political history. Media and identity courses drawing on American material supply comparative methods. Political philosophy, comparative politics, international relations and conflict anchor the distinct third option. The active workbook was searched for European languages, language instruction and progression in the named languages. Beginner Dutch and the study of linguistic structure, speech and bilingualism do not form a German or alternative European-language proficiency sequence. The comparison retains seven bounded pairings and leaves the specialist German modules, linguistic methods, minor and thesis unmatched.

alignment.rationale: Both examine linguistic structure, including word and sentence patterns. UCR applies this to meaning in texts, while Groningen compares the structures of European languages.
Both study how the mind processes language. Groningen focuses on psycho- and neurolinguistic research methods.
Both analyse how stories shape identity. UCR focuses on memoir, autobiography and travel writing.
Both interpret and produce narratives. UCR works in the specific form of nonfiction film.
Both introduce the interpretation of literature. Groningen places texts in a European cultural context.
Both examine modern European history. Groningen also introduces linguistic and political ways to study Europe.
Both examine democracy and political institutions. UCR uses a wider comparative scope.

Groningen introduces European language and society as a dedicated field.
Groningen continues the German sequence through formal written and spoken communication.
Groningen develops academic skills in the context of the programme profiles.
The third German course develops academic communication at C1.
Groningen reserves 10 EC for a choice within the programme’s profile and language options.
Groningen applies linguistic analysis to Standard German.
Groningen examines first- and second-language learning through theory and research.
Groningen analyses literary genres and periods in German.
Groningen studies German political culture and its European context in the major language.

This advanced German module brings together linguistics, literature and politics.

Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. The optional UCR research shown alongside it is separate from the course schedules.
